content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name], so I appreciate your patience. For my project, I need to monitor 17 analog inputs and control 2 analog plus 2 digital outputs. From what I've found, it seems you can't use more than 8 analog inputs. Is this a hard limit? Are there any options to go beyond this? If I switch 6 analog sensors to digital ones, the signals would be square pulses between 0-400 Hz. Is it feasible to process these signals using a [product_name]?

The numbers you've mentioned are the maximum supported by the system. The internal cycle time of [product_name] affects how well it can manage pulsing signals. Processing 6 signals at 400 Hz isn't recommended, as program complexity and size influence the number of signals that can be reliably handled. You could consider using multiple units in a network, which also allows positioning closer to your field devices. Alternatively, investigating remote Modbus TCP stations might be worthwhile, although I can't personally confirm if it'll meet your needs.

Hi [user_name], What you're referring to is indeed the maximum number of inputs and outputs that a single [product_name] supports, as outlined in the manual. When expansion modules are added, you can increase the number of inputs/outputs to the maximum configuration. It's possible for [product_name] units to communicate with each other—up to 8 total—and exchange input/output data, which can help expand your setup. You might want to look into the maximum network configuration described for [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing challenges due to input limitations in [product_name], specifically the maximum analog inputs allowed per device. The technical constraints seem fixed by the manual, and the system's cycle time further restricts processing high-frequency digital inputs. Suggestions include networking multiple devices or utilizing expansion modules, but the core need for additional analog inputs in a single device remains unfulfilled.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to expand the system to support more than 8 analog inputs and reliably handle digital signals up to 400 Hz, ideally within a single device.
